{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2022}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=November 2022}} {{Infobox football match | title = 2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final | image = Croke park hogan stand.jpg | image_size = 200 | event = [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] | team1association = [[File:Colours of Limerick.svg|40px]] | team1score = 0–30 | team2 = [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] | team2association = [[File:Colours of Kilkenny.svg|40px]] | team2score = 2–15 | date = 23 July 2023 | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Peter Casey (hurler)|Peter Casey]]{{cite news|url=https://hoganstand.com/article/index/328610|title=Casey scoops 'Man of the Match' award|work=Hogan Stand|date=24 July 2023}} | referee = John Keenan ([[Wicklow GAA|Wicklow]]) | weather = Cloudy with a moderate to fresh northerly breeze
{{convert|17|°C|°F|abbr=on}}{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0720/1395643-all-ireland-hurling-final-all-you-need-to-know/|title=All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final: All you need to know|publisher=[[RTÉ News]]|first=Declan|last=Whooley|date=23 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}} | attendance = 82,300 | previous = [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2022]] | next = [[2024 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2024]] }} The '''2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 23 July 2023{{Cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/football/2022/0924/1325285-league-finals-retained-as-2023-calendar-takes-shape/|title=League finals retained as 2023 calendar takes shape|date=24 September 2022|via=www.rte.ie}}{{Cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Meath/Article/Index/325123|title=Allianz League finals retained while All-Ireland SFC extended by one week - HoganStand|website=hoganstand.com}} between [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] and [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]], the culmination of the [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|136th final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. Reigning title holder Limerick won the game by 0–30 to 2–15 to claim their four-in-a-row and their fifth title in six years.{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/four-in-a-row-glory-for-limerick-as-treaty-take-down-kilkenny-with-devastating-all-ireland-final-blitz/a484829423.html|title=Four in-a-row glory for Limerick as Treaty take down Kilkenny with devastating All-Ireland final blitz|publisher=[[Irish Independent]]|first=Sean|last=McGoldrick|date=23 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}}{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0723/1396051-limericks-leaders-rally-to-roar-past-cats/|title=Leaders drive Limerick past Kilkenny to four in a row|publisher=[[RTÉ News]]|first=Eoin|last=Ryan|date=23 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}} The match was televised live on [[RTÉ2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'', presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]] from the Croke Park studio with analysis by [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]], [[Dónal Óg Cusack]] and [[Liam Sheedy]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]].{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0723/1396005-all-ireland-hurling-final-limerick-v-kilkenny-updates/|title=All-Ireland hurling final recap: Limerick beat Kilkenny to seal four-in-a-row|publisher=[[RTÉ News]]|first=Raf|last=Diallo|date=23 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}} BBC Northern Ireland covered the final for the first time as part of the Championship, previously BBC just covered football and not Hurling. Their coverage was presented by Thomas Niblock with commentary is by Oisin Langan, with pitch-side updates from Sarah Mulkerrins.{{Cite web | title=BBC Two - The Championship, 2023: All-Ireland Hurling Championship, Final: Limerick v Kilkenny | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m001p4lq | access-date=2026-08-14 | website=www.bbc.co.uk}} The match drew a peak audience of more than 1 million on RTÉ. The TV audience for ''The Sunday Game'' coverage peaked at 1,125,000 by the end of the final, the highest since 2019.{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0724/1396233-over-1-million-watch-limericks-four-in-a-row-success/|title=Over 1 million watch Limerick's four-in-a-row success|publisher=[[RTÉ News]]|date=24 July 2023|accessdate=24 July 2023}} ==Background== {{main|Kilkenny–Limerick hurling rivalry}} *[[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] were aiming to complete a four-in-a-row, having won the All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championships of [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2020]], [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2021]] and [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2022]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-keep-all-ireland-four-in-a-row-dream-alive-after-semi-final-surge-blows-galway-away/a269872893.html|title=Limerick keep All-Ireland four in-a-row dream alive after semi-final surge blows Galway away|date=8 July 2023|website=Independent.ie}} This had only been done twice before in the championship's history, by [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] in [[1941 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1941]]–[[1944 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|44]] and [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] in [[2006 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2006]]–[[2009 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|09]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20275116.html|title=Ring's 1944 goal opened door to four-in-a-row|first=Richard|last=Fitzpatrick|date=11 July 2014|website=Irish Examiner}} *[[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] were aiming to win their first All-Ireland since [[2015 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2015]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.breakingnews.ie/sport/gaa-preview-all-ireland-hurling-final-and-camogie-quarter-finals-1334931.html|title=GAA preview: All-Ireland Hurling final and Camogie quarter-finals|date=13 July 2022|website=BreakingNews.ie}} *This was to be the tenth Kilkenny–Limerick final; Limerick had won five of these ([[1897 All-Ireland Championship final|1973]], [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2022]]) and Kilkenny four ([[1933 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1933]], [[1935 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1935]], [[1974 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1974]], [[2007 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2007]]).{{Cite He previously refereed the [[2016 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|2016 All-Ireland minor final]], the [[2018 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship final|2018 All-Ireland Under-21 final]], the [[2019 Leinster Senior Hurling Championship final|2019 Leinster hurling final]] and the [[2022 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2022 Munster hurling final]]. His umpires were Tommy Redmond (Tinahely), Eddie Leonard (St Patrick's), Paul Reville (Turin) and David Clune (Delvin). His linemen were Galway's Liam Gordon and Wexford's James Owens, with Gordon also the standby referee. The sideline official was Shane Hynes from Galway.{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/john-keenan-appointed-as-referee-for-all-ireland-hurling-final/a1451886422.html|title= John Keenan appointed as referee for All-Ireland hurling final|date=13 July 2023|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=18 July 2023}} ===Build-up=== Both teams confirmed that they would return home to their respective counties straight after the match and not remain in Dublin overnight. Limerick would return to Fitzgerald's Woodlands House Hotel and Spa in [[Adare]] while Kilkenny would go to the River Court Hotel in Kilkenny. {{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0718/1395171-no-capital-stay-for-kilkenny-limerick-on-night-of-final/|title= No post-game banquet for Kilkenny or Limerick in the capital after All-Ireland hurling final|date=19 July 2023|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=19 July 2023}} The final was shown on a big screen on [[Pery Square]] in Limerick where an all ticket crowd watched the match.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerick.ie/council/newsroom/news/all-ireland-big-screen-event-in-limerick-city-centre|title=All Ireland Big Screen event in Limerick City Centre|website=[[Limerick.ie]]|date=18 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}} ===Jubilee teams=== The [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] team that won the [[1998 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1998 All-Ireland Final]] was presented to the crowd before the match.{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/advice-for-supporters-attending-the-all-ireland-shc-final/|title= Advice for supporters attending the All-Ireland SHC Final|date=23 July 2023|work=GAA.ie|accessdate=24 July 2023}} ==Match== ===Summary=== [[Paddy Deegan]] opened the scoring for Kilkenny in the opening minute of the game, a lead which was held for a further five minutes before Limerick could equalise through [[Cian Lynch]], this would be the only time the sides were level until deep into the second half. Limerick would for a brief moment, take the lead of the game when [[Diarmaid Byrnes]] knocked over Limerick's second point of the afternoon. However, Limerick's bright start was negated when, in the 10th minute, [[Eoin Cody]] picked up a loose ball in the Limerick box, and tucked it low into the bottom-right of the Limerick net, giving Kilkenny a two point advantage. By the 14th minute, two of Limerick's half-back line, [[William O'Donoghue]] and [[Diarmaid Byrnes]] received yellow cards for foul play. Kilkenny would go on to dominate much of the first half proceedings, leading by as much as six points by the 27th minute. At the end of the first half, Kilkenny led by three points on a 1-09 to 0-09 scoreline. Limerick started the second half intensely, rejuvenating their hopes of a fourth successive championship, bringing the scores to within a point by the 40th minute. Yet the afternoon was about to take another turn when a piece of individual brilliance saw Deegan scored a goal for Kilkenny, breaking the right side-netting of the Limerick goal. This saw Kilkenny extend their lead to five points in the 42nd minute. Limerick would bravely respond to this turn of events, aggressively seeking possession and scoring five successive points to bring the scores level for only the second time in the contest with 13 minutes remaining in normal time. From this point onwards, Limerick took control of proceedings, taking the lead for the first time since the sixth minute, when [[Darragh O'Donovan]] made it 0-18 to 2-11 in the 58th minute. In total, Limerick outscored Kilkenny 0-21 to 1-06 in the second half, completing a stellar comeback and running out comfortable winners. The game finished Kilkenny 2-15 (21 points), Limerick 0-30 (30 points). This fourth consecutive championship meant Limerick became only the third county, since the competition began in 1887, to win four All-Ireland hurling titles in a row.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41189653.html|title=Magnificent Limerick ignite in second half to make history|publisher=[[Irish Examiner]]|first=John|last=Fogarty|date=23 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}}{{cite news|url=https://www.breakingnews.ie/sport/all-ireland-hurling-final-kilkenny-lead-limerick-by-three-points-at-half-time-1506011.html|title=Limerick come back to beat Kilkenny and win fourth All-Ireland in a row|publisher=[[BreakingNews.ie]]|first=James|last=Cox|date=23 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/all-ireland-shc-final-limerick-produce-stunning-second-half-display-to-retain-ti/|title=All-Ireland SHC Final: Limerick produce stunning second half display to retain title|website=[[GAA.ie]]|first=Cian|last=O'Connell|date=23 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023}} While David Blanchfield was named on the Kilkenny squad to start at right wing back, he was unable to due to injury. Walter Walsh started in the position instead wearing the number 24 jersey. While starting in the half back line, Walsh operated across the half forward line, with Conor Fogarty dropping back to cover the number 5 position, and John Donnelly occupying the midfield area.
